memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses said to God, "Suppose I go to the Israelites and say to them, 'The God of your fathers has sent me to you,' and they ask me, 'What is his name?' Then what shall I tell them?" God said to Moses, "I am who I am. This is what you are to say to the Israelites: 'I am has sent me to you.'"" - Exodus 3:13-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses asks for a name, and God gives him one of the most profound sentences in all Scripture: I AM WHO I AM.

Every other name depends on something else. We are sons and daughters, employees, citizens — defined by relationships and roles. God is defined by nothing outside Himself. He simply is. He was never created, never developed, never depends on anyone. He is the one self-existing, unchanging reality behind everything that exists.

For a slave people whose world was collapsing, this was solid ground. Pharaohs come and go. Empires rise and fall. I AM remains.

And then, fifteen centuries later, a carpenter from Nazareth stood before religious leaders and said, "Before Abraham was born, I am" (Jn 8:58). They picked up stones, because they understood exactly what He was claiming.

The God of the burning bush has a face, and it is the face of Jesus Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What in my life feels unstable, and how does the unchanging I AM steady me?
2. Do I take seriously who Jesus claimed to be?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Eternal God, You alone never change. When everything around me shifts, anchor me in who You are. Amen.
